title: Pictorial Atlas of a Girl Who Cut a Library into Pieces

description.main: A two-volume artist's book by Czech artist Eva Koťátková (b. 1982), staging roughly 300 collages as an imagined 1980s schoolbook from her Prague childhood under Communist rule, paired with a documentary volume of real Czechoslovak institutional regulations from 1961-1989.
description.extended:
Pictorial Atlas of a Girl Who Cut a Library into Pieces is a two-volume artist's book by the Czech artist Eva Koťátková (b. 1982), staging roughly 300 collages as an imagined 1980s schoolbook from her Prague childhood under Communist rule.

Co-published in 2016 by JRP|Editions and tranzit.cz — the twelfth volume in tranzit's series on Central and Eastern European artists — the book gathers collages and drawings made 2013–2015: children at play or bound into diagrams, spliced with anatomical fragments and puppet-like armatures, in scenes with the psychological unease of Kafka. A companion volume, Institutional, Operational and Organisational Rules and Regulations 1961–1989, reprints twenty-two sets of real Czechoslovak bureaucratic regulations, pairing Koťátková's invented pedagogy with the actual machinery of state control it echoes.

Koťátková studied at the San Francisco Art Institute and the Academy of Fine Arts in Prague, and works across collage, sculpture, and performance to examine how institutions discipline the body and imagination of children. Her work has appeared in the 2013 and 2024 Venice Biennales and documenta fifteen; she is represented by Hunt Kastner (Prague) and Meyer Riegger (Berlin/Karlsruhe).
description.artist_bio: Eva Koťátková (b. 1982, Prague) is a Czech installation artist whose practice spans sculpture, collage, video, and performance, dealing with surveillance and control of the body, psychology, and institutional power. She studied at the San Francisco Art Institute and the Academy of Fine Arts in Prague. Her work has been shown at the 2013 Venice Biennale, documenta fifteen (2022), and the Czech and Slovak Pavilion at the 2024 Venice Biennale. She is represented by Hunt Kastner (Prague), Meyer Riegger (Berlin/Karlsruhe), and Maccarone (New York).

notes: Page count conflicts across sources: co-publisher tranzit.cz lists 712 pp for the two-volume set, JRP|Editions' own product page lists 703 pp, and DAP/artbook.com lists 400 pp (likely counting a single volume). Used tranzit.cz's 712 pp figure as the direct co-publisher and closest to JRP's own number. Publication year also varies (JRP: January 2016; tranzit.cz: 2015); used JRP's 2016, matching the internationally distributed ISBN 9783037643617. The book is a two-volume slipcased set; the second volume's full title is 'Institutional, Operational and Organisational Rules and Regulations 1961-1989' — folded into the description rather than the title field, matching how JRP/DAP/Amazon/B&N market the title. No personal official website found for the artist; authors[0].url uses her primary Prague gallery, Hunt Kastner.
